evidence: Read cold in 'Before you begin', the paragraph about a safe place and when not to do this. DRAFT: 'If you are already partially or fully opened, use the later 'Already open? Contain before you deepen' section to help orient yourself, but do not attempt to deepen yourself if you are not stable.' CHANGE CHECK: against the words SOURCE.txt says it replaces, the only difference is the deleted 'you can' ('you can use' becomes 'use'). The heading's own words, 'later' and 'not stable' are all there, so it does what the_change says. Worth knowing for whoever shows it to the author: the net edit is that one cut, so the marking card should describe it as that and not as a fresh rewrite of the whole sentence; whether it moves a detector is Pangram's question, not this review's. MEANING: SOURCE.txt's card says the later Already open? practice is for orientation, not permission to intensify an unstable state. The draft says use that section to orient, and do not deepen if you are not stable. That is the same rule. Nothing is added: no new claim, study, person or first-person fact (C03, C04 absent). Turning 'you can use' into 'use' makes the pointer a direction instead of an option; in a safety line that is acceptable and not a change of meaning. FLOW AND REFERENTS: it follows the sentence before it (if you are intoxicated, acutely confused or unable to keep yourself safe, get support instead of exploratory hypnosis) as the next safety case, someone who is already open, and gives that person somewhere to go. 'yourself' is the reader both times. 'the later ... section' names its target by its heading. I could not open the article to confirm that heading exists, but SOURCE.txt's card refers to 'The later Already open? practice' and the replaced words quote the same heading, so it is consistent with everything I was given. Reading notes, none a fail: 'opened' is jargon that this page never explains, but the quoted heading 'Already open?' answers it for the reader; 'do not attempt to' is a little more formal than 'Don’t do this if you’re driving' two sentences earlier, which reads as warning emphasis and is the same wording the replaced sentence had. TELL ROWS: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal draft in its context and found none actually happening. Closest calls: T02, because the paragraph is a run of 'if you are X, do Y' safety cases. But they are separate real situations (driving or water; intoxicated or confused; already open), the other three correspond to his published safety lines in the SOURCE.txt card, this change leaves the cadence exactly as it was, and its own sentence carries a counter-consideration (use the section, but do not deepen if unstable). T11 and T19, because it points at a later section: it carries a safety instruction and not just a signpost. T06, for 'orient yourself' and 'stable': these are the article's own terms and match the card. T26, for 'deepen' twice and 'yourself' twice: the caution deliberately picks up the heading's word and the reflexive is parallel, so the repeat does a job. T17, for 'Contain before you deepen': that is his own heading, quoted, not a thesis in the draft's voice. T22: the coach cushion in the replaced sentence was 'you can', and it is gone. LINTER FINDINGS: (a) 'D9 follows the source order', 1 of 1 paragraphs. A one-sentence change whose order (condition, pointer, caution) is fixed by what it says, so following the source's order is expected; the caution after 'but' is the noticing. Accepted. I am not relying on the writer's ADMISSION reason for this finding, which cites asides ('if I can put it that way', 'of course', 'just', '!') that are not in this draft. (b) 'E36/E41 heavy second person', 8.8 per 100 words (3 'you' in 34 words). The whole page speaks to the reader as 'you'; one of the three sits inside the quoted heading and the other two are the 'if you are' conditions of a safety line; and the coach cushion 'you can' that fed the coach-register concern is already cut. Accepted. Verdict PASS: it does what the_change says, keeps the source meaning, adds nothing, has no unjustified tell, and reads right where it sits.
